findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the back door of the facility to be slightly open. A window with no screen was also open. PIC was informed that outer openings of the facility need to be protected to prevent the entry of insects and rodents.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

Repeat Violation

Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to avoid cross-contamination.

Observed a mop stored in the bottom of a dump sink in the back maintenance area. PIC was informed that mop heads need to be stored hanging so that they can drip dry. findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
7501200 & 1220 - A) Glue traps with varying amounts of debris and dead roach accumulation were observed throughout the facility. Remove the old glue traps. Replace glue traps frequently/as needed to allow for proper functioning of traps. 

B) Floor around water heater and furnace was soiled. Clean the floor in the water heater/furnace closet

C) The floor in the dish area was observed with the following conditions:
1. around the grease trap was soiled with food debris and some dead roaches;
2. glue trap full of debris and dead roaches was observed under the 3 part sink near the grease trap;   and
3. food/debris accumulation was observed in a gap along the juncture where the baseboard and floor tiles meet under the 3 part sink.
Thorough, detail cleaning is needed in the dish area around the grease trap and along the floor to wall juncture under the 3 part sink/behind the grease trap. Once detail cleaning is completed, all gaps need to be properly sealed.

D) Terminix trap in the electrical closet had a dead mouse in it. Remove the trap and properly dispose of the contents.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed.'

C) Flour and cob web accumulation were observed on the wall behind the mixers and the outer wall of the walkin freezer. The condensate pump motor was also heavily oiled with flour accumulation. findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Bianco sauce (containing minced garlic) had surface and internal temperatures of 58F and 60F. Owner noted the products are made daily, and the sauce was from yesterday. Bianco sauce was discarded in the trash during the inspection.

Cold potentially hazardous foods must be maintained at 41F/below during storage. Portions of the aforementioned product may be removed from cold holding in advance to allow for ease in dispensing and left out if time control is used (product used/discarded w/in 4hrs).

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Pizza sauce in two door cooler prepared the previous operating day had surface and internal temperatures of 51F and 55F-56F. Sauce was in a 10gal plastic container. Sauce was discarded in the dumpster during the inspection. Owner noted the recipe requires hot water be used to prepare the sauce, so pre-chilling ingredients is not a valid option. Owner plans to use smaller pans for portioning sauce and allowing for more rapid cooling. Owner was advised to also utilize ice baths and stir the sauce frequently as well. Another option would be to portion in smaller pans and place cooling product uncovered on the top shelf in the walkin cooler or walkin freezer temporarily to help rapidly drop temperature. 

Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/ w/in an additional 4 hrs. Total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs.
Any product prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature must be cooled to 41F/below w/in 4hrs. The only way to know foods are reaching benchmark temperatures in designated time frame is to use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to monitor the temperature during the cooling process. Do not cool foods at room temperature.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.153 - Container of sauce was sitting out at prep area. Facility uses time control, but the time was not marked on the container. Employee spoke with owner via phone upon arrival of inspector. Sauce had been out since ~12p. Benefit of doubt was given. Time was marked on the container to indicate the product needed to be discarded by 4pm. Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Mark the time on the sauce so it is clear when the product was removed from cold holding and when the product needs to be discarded. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Soufflé cup of sauce in hot holding well was 113F. Soufflé cups of sauce were discarded in the trash. Owner stated the portions of sauce would be held cold in the walkin and heated in the microwave as needed. Hot foods shall be maintained at 135F/above at all times. If portions of sauce are to be held in warmer then time control may be applied, and soufflé cups of sauce must be sold or discarded w/in 4hrs.
